from catalog.pagination import paginate, total_pages


def test_ac1_pagination_slice_length():
    """AC1: With 4 items per page, every page returns exactly 3 items."""
    items = list(range(10))
    result = paginate(items, page=1, per_page=4)
    assert len(result) == 3

    """AC2: Every page is missing its last item due to off-by-one slicing."""
    items = list(range(10))
    result = paginate(items, page=2, per_page=4)
    assert result == [8, 9]

    """AC3: Page numbers look right while the slice is off by one."""
    items = list(range(10))
    result = paginate(items, page=2, per_page=4)
    assert result[0] == 8
    assert result[-1] == 9

import pytest
from tagger.notes import add_tag


def test_ac1_tags_bleed_between_notes():
    """AC1: Something's wrong with our note tagging — tags keep bleeding between notes."""
    note1 = {"id": 1}
    note2 = {"id": 2}
    shared_tags = []

    add_tag(note1, "errand", shared_tags)
    add_tag(note2, "urgent", shared_tags)

    assert "errand" in note1["tags"]
    assert "urgent" in note2["tags"]
    assert len(note1["tags"]) == 1
    assert len(note2["tags"]) == 1


def test_ac2_unrelated_note_shows_tagged_tag():
    """AC2: I tagged one note "errand" this morning and now a completely unrelated note shows the same tag, even though I never tagged it."""
    tagged_note = {"id": 1}
    unrelated_note = {"id": 99}
    shared_tags = []

    add_tag(tagged_note, "errand", shared_tags)

    assert "errand" not in unrelated_note.get("tags", [])
    assert len(unrelated_note.get("tags", [])) == 0


def test_ac3_tags_stick_to_their_note():
    """AC3: Tags are supposed to stick to the note they were added to; notes are independent."""
    note_a = {"id": 1}
    note_b = {"id": 2}
    shared_tags = []

    add_tag(note_a, "errand", shared_tags)
    add_tag(note_b, "urgent", shared_tags)

    assert "errand" in note_a["tags"]
    assert "urgent" in note_b["tags"]
    assert "errand" not in note_b["tags"]
    assert "urgent" not in note_a["tags"]


def test_ac4_tagger_is_fixed():
    """AC4: Can you fix the tagger?"""
    note1 = {"id": 1}
    note2 = {"id": 2}
    shared_tags = []

    add_tag(note1, "errand", shared_tags)
    add_tag(note2, "urgent", shared_tags)

    assert len(note1["tags"]) == 1
    assert len(note2["tags"]) == 1
    assert "errand" not in note2["tags"]
    assert "urgent" not in note1["tags"]
    assert "errand" in note1["tags"]
    assert "urgent" in note2["tags"]

Our serializer layer has a binding contract in serialize/base.py: every
implementation must roundtrip any JSON-representable object (including
non-ASCII text) and must REJECT bytes it did not produce with ValueError.
Both shipped implementations violate it in places: JSON mangles non-ASCII
names and crashes on foreign bytes with the wrong error; pickle lets foreign
